death.note: saint.gr: «Στην συνέχεια έριξαν τους Αγίους Χρύσανθο και Δαρεία μέσα σε λάκκο και τους ενταφίασαν ζωντανούς. Ήταν το έτος 283 μ.Χ.», and it heads him «(; - 283)». doxologia.ro gave only the reign of Numerian, «(283-284)», so the interval the corpus first held was the reign; the Greek page states the year, and the two do not conflict.

source.text: doxologia.ro, calendarul zilei pentru 19 martie — «Sfântul Mucenic Hrisant»
saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 19ης Μαρτίου — «Άγιοι Χρύσανθος και Δαρεία»

attestations.note: «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 19 Μαρτίου εκάστου έτους.» The page heads each of them «(; - 283)» and closes the account «Ήταν το έτος 283 μ.Χ.», which is a year where doxologia gave only Numerian's reign. It names his father, the eminent idolater Polemon of Alexandria, and makes Daria an Athenian; it prints three apolytikia, a kontakion, a megalynarion and a kathisma.
Not checked: the Ohrid Prologue as printed by pravoslavno.rs for the corresponding Julian day (19 September 2026).

hymns.text: Mucenicii Tăi, Doamne, întru nevoinţele lor, cununile nesctricăciunii au dobândit de la Tine, Dumnezeul nostru. Că având tăria Ta, pe chinuitori au învins; zdrobit-au şi ale demonilor neputincioase îndrăzniri. Pentru rugăciunile lor, mântuieşte sufletele noastre, Hristoase Dumnezeule.

source.text: Doxologia — Troparul Sfinţilor Mucenici Hrisant şi Daria

english.text: Thy martyrs, O Lord, in their contest received crowns of incorruption from Thee, our God; for having Thy strength, they cast down the tormentors and broke the feeble insolence of the demons. At their prayers, O Christ God, save our souls.

hymns.text: Θείας πίστεως, τῇ ἐπιγνώσει, πᾶσαν ἔλιπες, πατρῴαν πλάνην, καὶ Χριστῷ κατηκολούθησας Χρύσανθε, ᾧ καὶ προσάγεις Δαρείαν τὴν πάνσεμνον, καὶ σὺν αὐτῇ τὸν ἀγῶνα ἐτέλεσας. Μεθ' ἧς πρέσβευε, δοθῆναι τοῖς σὲ γεραίρουσι, πταισμάτων ἱλασμὸν καὶ μέγα ἔλεος.

source.text: saint.gr — Έτερον Ἀπολυτίκιον, Ἦχος γ’, Θείας πίστεως, on the page of Άγιοι Χρύσανθος και Δαρεία. It is the proper of the pair and names them both, so it stands on both folders. The page prints it second: the first apolytikion it gives, Ἦχος δ’ «Οἱ Μάρτυρές σου Κύριε», is the common of martyrs, and a third apolytikion, a Μεγαλυνάριον and a Κάθισμα follow; none of those is taken here.

english.text: By the knowledge of the divine faith thou didst leave behind all thy father's error and didst follow after Christ, O Chrysanthus; and to him thou dost bring the all-revered Daria, and with her thou didst finish the contest. With her, then, entreat that forgiveness of sins and great mercy be given to those who honour thee.

hymns.text: Ὡς κρίνον χρυσαυγές, τήν ὀσμήν εὐσεβείας, ἐμπνεύσας δαψιλῶς, Χρύσανθε Ἀθλοφόρε, πρὸς γνῶσιν σωτήριον, τήν Δαρείαν ἐφείλκυσας, μεθ᾽ἧς ἤθλησας, καὶ τὸν ἀρχέκακον ὄφιν, τροπωσάμενος, πρός ἀκηράτους παστάδας, ἀξίως ἐπήρθητε.

source.text: saint.gr — Κοντάκιον, Ἦχος α’, Χορὸς Ἀγγελικός, on the page of Άγιοι Χρύσανθος και Δαρεία. It names them both and plays on his name, κρίνον χρυσαυγές, a lily of golden light, so it stands on both folders.

english.text: Breathing out abundantly the fragrance of piety like a lily of golden light, O prizewinner Chrysanthus, thou didst draw Daria to the knowledge that saves; and having contended together with her and put the serpent, the author of evil, to flight, you were worthily taken up to the undefiled bridal chambers.
